title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Term 3. Term 4 is set aside for revision and the final examinations.
This question paper consists of 3 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 250 000 map, a road is 6,4 cm long. What is its real length in km?
A 15 m wall is drawn as 10 cm on a plan. What is the scale?
A 1 : 40 scale model of a 6 m long bus is built. How long is the model, in cm?
3,4 hours is the same as 3 hours 40 minutes.
questions.explanation: 0,4 h = 24 minutes, so 3,4 h = 3 h 24 min.

questions.prompt: A taxi owner drives 85 km each way to work, 22 days a month. The taxi uses 11 ℓ/100 km and diesel costs R22,90/ℓ. Calculate the monthly fuel cost.
A bus leaves Durban at 21:30 and travels 600 km to Johannesburg at an average of 75 km/h, with a 40-minute stop. When does it arrive?
questions.memo:
✓ 600 ÷ 75 = 8 h (1)
✓ + 40 min = 8 h 40 min (1)
✓ Arrives 06:10 the next day (1)

questions.prompt: Why are both a floor plan and an elevation plan needed to calculate how much paint is needed for the walls of a room?
questions.memo:
✓ The floor plan gives the lengths of the walls (1)
✓ The elevation plan gives the heights, so the wall area can be calculated (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Data Handling: Interpretation and Critical Analysis

questions.prompt: A learner's mark is at the 90th percentile. This means…
options: she did better than about 90% of learners

questions.prompt: The lower quartile is the same as the…
In a negative relationship, as one variable increases the other tends to decrease.
Monthly rents in a block of flats: R4 200; R4 500; R4 500; R4 800; R5 100; R12 000. Find the median rent.
School A: median 58%, IQR 24. School B: median 63%, IQR 10. Compare the two schools' results.
questions.memo:
✓ School B performed better on average (higher median) (2)
✓ School B's results are more consistent (smaller IQR) (1)
✓ School A has a wider spread of marks (1)

questions.prompt: A trend line shows the population of a town growing by 2 000 people per year from 2015 to 2024. Why is it risky to use it to predict the population in 2060?
questions.memo:
✓ 2060 is far outside the data range (extrapolation) (1)
✓ Growth rates can change because of economic, social or migration factors (1)

questions.prompt: A forecast gives a 20% chance of rain. Which is the best interpretation?
options: It will rain for 20% of the day
On days like this, it rains about 1 in 5 times
20% of the area will get rain

questions.prompt: A game costs R5. You win R30 with a probability of $\frac{1}{8}$. What is the expected value per game, in rand? (use a minus sign for a loss)
The probability that a component fails is 0,1. Two independent components are used. What is P(at least one fails)?
Buying more lottery tickets every week is a reliable way to grow your savings.
In a study, 6 out of 1 000 smokers and 1 out of 1 000 non-smokers developed a disease. Calculate the relative risk and explain what it means.
questions.memo:
✓ 0,6% and 0,1% (1)
✓ Relative risk = 6 (1)
✓ Smokers were 6 times as likely to develop the disease (1)

questions.prompt: A spinner has 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5. It costs R4 to play and you win R15 if it lands on 5. Is the game fair? Show working.
questions.memo:
✓ P(5) = $\frac{1}{5}$ (1)
✓ Expected winnings $\frac{1}{5} \times R15 = R3$ (1)
✓ R3 < R4, so not fair: the player expects to lose R1 per game (1)

questions.prompt: Why might a positive result on a test for a rare disease still be likely to be a false positive?
questions.memo:
✓ Because the disease is rare, most people tested do not have it (1)
✓ so even a small error rate produces more false positives than true positives (1)
